name: Methiodone
addictionPotential: highly addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

summary: A synthetic opioid analgesic and structural analogue of methadone, in which the ketone group is replaced by an ethyl sulfone group. It acts as a μ-opioid receptor agonist with potency approximately 0.5–1.0x that of methadone.
effectsSummary: Effects develop slowly and produce a warm, sedation-heavy maintenance-like opioid feeling rather than acute euphoria.
dosageRemark: The powder can be caustic and irritating to mucous membranes; oral ingestion via capsule or dilute solution is strongly recommended over nasal administration. Sensitivity varies significantly between individuals, so always begin with an allergy test and low dose.
generalRisks: As a potent opioid depressant, high doses carry severe risks of fatal respiratory depression. Accumulates in the body with consecutive daily use; wait at least 12 hours before re-dosing. Potential risk of QT interval prolongation similar to methadone.
saferUse: Never combine with alcohol, benzodiazepines, GHB, or other CNS depressants due to fatal respiratory depression risk.
Potent opioids carry extreme addiction and physical dependence risks; avoid frequent or continuous daily use.
Has a long elimination half-life and accumulates in the body; wait at least 12 hours between doses.
Keep naloxone accessible when researching or using novel opioids.
metabolism: Human metabolism has not yet been formally established in modern clinical trials. As a sulfone bioisostere of methadone, hepatic clearance and CYP enzymes are presumed to be involved. Consecutive daily dosing leads to accumulation due to a prolonged half-life.
